The core insight is that abstention feedback introduces a dual learning problem: simultaneously inferring the classifier and the abstention behavior. This is modeled via a joint Bayesian posterior over label functions h and abstention functions r. The key innovation lies in the BALAF framework which updates both h and r upon labeling and only r upon abstention. The greedy criteria ALa and ALw are derived from maximizing expected version-space reduction under this joint structure. ALa uses an information-theoretic formulation akin to Gibbs error but adjusted for abstention, while ALw adopts a worst-case confidence measure. Both rules inherit submodularity properties—adaptive for ALa and pointwise for ALw—which yield (1-1/e) approximation guarantees. These primitives enable GSE to intelligently allocate its research budget by avoiding queries where abstention is likely, and focusing on those that reduce joint uncertainty most effectively.
